senses.d: The part of a plant, generally underground, that anchors and supports the plant body, absorbs and stores water and nutrients, and in some plants is able to perform vegetative reproduction.

A root caught Ulot's left foot and he almost fell.

senses.d: A root vegetable.
The part of a tooth extending into the bone holding the tooth in place.
ex: Root damage is a common problem of overbrushing.

senses.d: The part of a hair under the skin that holds the hair in place.
ex: The root is the only part of the hair that is alive.

senses.d: The part of a hair near the skin that has not been dyed, permed, or otherwise treated.
ex: He dyed his hair black last month, so the grey roots can be seen.

senses.d: The primary source; origin.
ex: The love of money is the root of all evil.

senses.d: The section of a wing immediately adjacent to the fuselage.

senses.d: Of a number or expression, a number which, when raised to a specified power, yields the specified number or expression.
ex: The cube root of 27 is 3.

senses.d: A square root (understood if no power is specified; in which case, “the root of” is often abbreviated to “root”).

senses.d: To grow roots; to enter the earth, as roots; to take root and begin to grow.
ex: The cuttings are starting to root.

senses.d: To prepare, oversee, or otherwise cause the rooting of cuttings.
ex: We rooted some cuttings last summer.

senses.d: To turn up or dig with the snout.
